title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipeline for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task) we produced a single shared initial candidate per task; the guarded artifact is the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered confirmatory large-effect hypothesis (sized for large absolute changes) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed. We reconcile estimand algebra, expand execution/accounting diagnostics, and supply deterministic artifact pointers and SHA‑256 digests for forensic verification.

sections.introduction: Modern LLMs can translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations, offering automation benefits in NetOps. However, incorrectly sequenced or malformed commands risk service disruption or policy violations. Production proposals therefore commonly interpose deterministic validators and limited automated repair loops as safety guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Prior empirical work in LLM→NetOps emphasizes generation accuracy but often omits preregistration, paired estimand clarity, or forensic artifact binding required for deterministic auditing. To address this gap we preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) and asked: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our principal contributions are (1) a preregistered paired estimand and confirmatory analysis, (2) deterministic per-episode validator traces and canonical ASTs enabling semantic checks, and (3) cryptographic digests and authoritative artifact paths that permit deterministic forensic reconstruction of contingency cells and the single repair event.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and static checking underpin modern NetOps validators. The canonical static-check technique is Header Space Analysis (Kazemian, Varghese, McKeown, 2012; see http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/summary?doi=10.1.1.228.5064), which enables precise forwarding- and policy-consistency reasoning before deployment. Incremental and online checkers such as VeriFlow (Khurshid et al., SIGCOMM 2013; DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452) extend these ideas to staged updates. Recent LLM→NetOps evaluations (e.g., NetConfEval [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296] and Lira et al., 2024 (DOI:10.1109/mcom.001.2400368)) measure generation accuracy and highlight failure modes—syntax drift, missing sequencing, and policy violations—but typically omit preregistration, shared-initial generation semantics, or per-episode deterministic traces. Work on generate–validate–repair architectures evaluates iterative repairs and verifier-assisted self-correction, but published experiments often lack strict adapter/repair budgets and forensic artifact binding. Our study situates itself between verification literature and LLM-driven NetOps evaluation by enforcing (a) shared_initial generation semantics, (b) a conservative repair budget (≤1 automated repair per task), (c) deterministic validator traces and canonical ASTs, and (d) cryptographic digests for full reproducibility.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered paired design (cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001; SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) specified N=200 intent→configuration tasks stratified by vendor family (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67). The primary_estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). The inferential test is an exact McNemar two-sided test plus a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed 1729).

Adapter contract and generation semantics. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false): one initial candidate per task was reused for both baseline and guarded conditions. The adapter permitted at most one automated repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1); provider-call accounting is archived (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891).

Synthetic task bank, validator, and scoring. Tasks were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each includes initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, group constraints), permitted touched fields, and an explicit required_sequence. The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses outputs into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax/parse, applies intent-constraint and dependency checks, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions. The validator emits per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before/after), a normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and a scoring flag using scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per-episode scoring JSONs and all raw results are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/raw_results.jsonl (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02). All artifact hashes appear in execution/execution_manifest.json (full manifest archived). 

Execution and missingness rules. The preregistered missingness policy allowed up to two automatic retries for failed provider calls; unresolved calls would remove the affected pair from the primary analysis. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution summary (execution manifest): planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions), completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair). Representative per-episode scoring JSON snippets for six tasks are included in the archive (see execution/scoring/ examples with SHA-256 digests in the manifest). 

Analysis pipeline. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 consumed execution/raw_results.jsonl and produced the paired contingency counts (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00), exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and paired bootstrap CI for the absolute paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). Analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0) are archived.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b29e8624a2f72a35b0073a6ee7644daa85db4a7948a9fa75e276c6c3d).

Understanding the test outcome. The exact McNemar test conditions on discordant pairs (n_10 + n_01). Here discordant mass = 1 (n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0), so the two-sided exact test yields p = 1.0; with a single discordant observation the test lacks sensitivity and cannot reject the null. The bootstrap CI quantifies estimation uncertainty and bounds the plausible absolute paired improvement to ≤1.5 percentage points under the bootstrap assumptions.

Per-stratum accounting and artifact-grounded access. The preregistered stratification was Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67; execution completed with no deterministic exclusions, so observed per-stratum sample sizes equal planned strata (66 / 67 / 67). The overall baseline failure (the single actionable error) and the single repair invocation are recorded deterministically in the archived per-episode scoring JSONs and in execution/raw_results.jsonl. Auditors may deterministically extract: per‑vendor baseline/guarded success/failure counts and the exact discordant episode identifier (and its scoring JSON) from the archived files execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) together with execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json). Because these values are derivable without ambiguity from the archived JSONs, auditors can reconstruct them exactly; the repository paths and SHA-256 digests above are authoritative.

Provider-call accounting. analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}, which explains model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair). The single recorded repair corresponds to the single discordant-pair improvement (n_10 = 1); repair_applied flags are present in per-episode validator_trace JSONs so the repaired episode can be located and inspected deterministically in the archive.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained execution (synthetic 200-task bank; gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; single automated repair attempt), the guarded pipeline eliminated the single observed actionable misconfiguration (1→0). However, because baseline failures were exceptionally rare (1/200), the absolute room for improvement was small and the preregistered power calibration (targeted at large absolute effects) is not informative for this rare-failure regime. The contingency counts (n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0) and provider-call accounting (one repair invocation) make the corrective pathway transparent: almost every initial candidate satisfied full intent constraints and only a single repair changed an actionable outcome.

Design and measurement lessons. The projected power in the preregistration was calibrated for large absolute changes (≈0.15); with observed baseline_error = 0.005 the same design is underpowered for large-effect detection. Practical remedies include increasing N, oversampling high-difficulty strata, using cost-weighted estimands that up-weight rare catastrophic outcomes, or permitting larger automated repair budgets to measure diminishing returns. For operational decision-making in rare-failure regimes, cost-weighted loss functions or risk-threshold estimands are often more informative than raw proportions.

Failure-mode diagnostics and validator coverage. Per-episode validator_traces include violation codes and allow automated clustering of residual failure types (syntax/parse, sequencing/dependency, simulator-detected semantic/policy violations). In this run guarded residual actionable errors = 0, so the preregistered secondary hypothesis comparing residual error-type proportions is untestable as a confirmatory statement (H2 remains untestable here). Nonetheless the archived validator_traces permit exploratory taxonomy construction in future runs with higher residual error prevalence.

Reproducibility and forensic audit. All authoritative artifacts and SHA-256 digests required for deterministic auditing are published in the execution archive: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a), analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891). Auditors can extract per‑vendor success/failure counts and the explicit discordant episode identifier (and the scoring JSON for that episode) deterministically from these files; their SHA‑256 digests above locate the exact bytes used for the analysis.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered confirmatory large-effect hypothesis is not supported because observed baseline error prevalence was far smaller than assumed in power planning. We publish cryptographic digests and authoritative artifact paths for every principal input, provider call, per-episode validator_trace, and analysis output so auditors can reconstruct contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the exact repaired episode from archived evidence. Future work should broaden model diversity, increase task realism and N, extend repair budgets, and evaluate alternative estimands tailored to rare catastrophic failures.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are computable from archived artifacts but are not printed verbatim in the manuscript body; auditors can compute them deterministically using the provided SHA-256 pointers.
